recall_prompt: Say how you would find the coefficient of x¹¹ — the power of x in the general term, the r that gives 11, and the coefficient.
insider_note: Write the general term first and collect the powers of x into 26 − 5r; set it equal to 11, not to zero — this is not the term-independent question. The coefficient is everything except the x¹¹.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: General term and the power of x
steps.margin_note: First mark. (x²)¹³⁻ʳ gives x²⁶⁻²ʳ and (1/x³)ʳ gives x⁻³ʳ, so the power is 26 − 5r.
steps.memory_tip: (x²)¹³⁻ʳ and (1/x³)ʳ make the power 26 − 5r. Set it to 11, not to zero.

recall.must_convey: That the power of x in the general term is 26 − 5r, and 26 − 5r = 11 gives r = 3.

steps.why: Only one r gives x¹¹, so only one term contributes to its coefficient.
common_mistakes: Writing the power as 26 − 2r − 3r and then adding the 3r.

steps.label: Evaluate the coefficient
steps.memory_tip: r = 3: the coefficient is ¹³C₃ · 2¹⁰ · 3³ — everything except the x¹¹.

recall.must_convey: That the coefficient of x¹¹ is ¹³C₃·2¹⁰·3³ = 286 × 1024 × 27.
